statement: Partition split snapshot batching closes the final v10 collection-boundary gaps: grouping constructs its Map through a module-captured constructor, snapshot columns are a nonempty bounded dense own-data string array, snapshot rows are a bounded dense own-data record array under the canonical 64-row source-batch owner, and over-wide dimensions fail closed before copying/grouping/dispatch while per-child SQL batching still respects the SQLite bind-variable budget; all v10/v9 routing, batching, intrinsic, ordering and ownership semantics remain unchanged.

constraints.statement: Supersedes sealed partition-key-ordering-owner-completion-v10 after category-complete Copilot PR #96 review rejected exact v10 candidate tree for two production-semantic gaps: routeSplitSnapshotBatch used live new Map() after module load, allowing Map replacement to silently suppress dispatch; and snapshot row/column dimensions lacked a policy cap, allowing over-wide/unbounded copying and dispatch beyond the SQLite 32,766 bind-variable budget. Preserve v10 predicate/evidence unchanged.

Snapshot grouping constructs the internal map through a Map constructor captured at module initialization. Replacing globalThis.Map after module load cannot change grouping, seed hidden rows, suppress partition order, or alter dispatch.
Snapshot columns are a nonempty canonical dense own-data array of primitive strings with length at most 32,766. Zero-column and over-wide column sets fail closed before row copying or dispatch.

One routeSplitSnapshotBatch call accepts at most 64 canonical dense own-data rows before copy/grouping, matching the existing split snapshot producer cadence. The 64-row value has one owner in partition-split-routing and PartitionService consumes that exported owner instead of restating a second literal.

Bounded dense-array copying is implemented by the existing strict-own-data owner via an optional max-length parameter; snapshot routing does not duplicate proxy/prototype/descriptor length semantics locally.

resolveSplitSnapshotBatchRowLimit rejects empty or over-wide column sets, preserves the existing min(requestedRows, floor(32,766 / columns)) per-SQL batching behavior, and the upstream split backfill obtains its 64-row request cap from the same routing owner.

Preserve v10 dense-own Proxy/sparse/accessor rejection, captured push/join/slice/get/set semantics, exact deterministic grouping/SQL/params, no silent row loss, preserved v9 closure, and all earlier routing/table-ID/evaluation-context/intrinsic semantics.

The exact rejected v10 candidate must be right-reason red for post-load global Map replacement, for a 65-row route call, and for a 32,767-column route call. The v11 candidate must make those controls plus v10/v11 closure and focused snapshot tests green, including the existing 64-row × 512-column 63+1 batching witness.
Existing KeyRangeManager intrinsic hardening remains a separate owner follow-up, unchanged by v11.
Persisted key type metadata, exact large-integer boundary representation, parser/bind precision, encoding migration and old-boundary revalidation remain A2.
Any v11 source candidate requires category-complete independent verification newer than its last attempt, covering both sealed verificationTemplates and exact candidate fingerprints.
No Raft runtime, consensus transport, lifecycle, membership or formation behavior changes.
